pa_install: ProjectArchitect 2.0 installed cleanly on Path A and Phase 0 closed with two trailer-free commits: the governance layout, docs layer, registry seed with §E reserved for the kit, CLAUDE.md, agent state with 16 seeded memories, a generated PROJECT_CONTEXT.md carrying the intake's eleven-phase ladder with one machine-checkable Milestone each, and PhaseEnd_Phase0.md with CURRENT_PHASE.md archived to phase-ends/logs/ — with §6 (global ~/.claude assets) skipped by instruction and Gate 2's effort toggle skipped as an unattended run.
commits: feat: Project Architect 2.0 installed — constitution generated
chore: decomp-architect Phase 0.5 — firewall, layout, bootstrap
chore: decomp-architect Phase 0.5 — the decomp overlay installed

defects.step: Step 3.7 — the ignore probes (FOUND in run 1; FIXED by the coordinator; CONFIRMED FIXED in run 2)
defects.what: `.run/README.md` was ignored, so Step 4's README could not be tracked and Step 5's checkpoint commit — which lists it as an explicit path — would have been refused. The kit's own block was correct in isolation (/.run/* + !/.run/README.md); ProjectArchitect's directory-form `.run/` above it vetoed the re-include, and git never descends into an excluded directory. The new Step 3.0 (rewrite that one line to /.run/*, the installer's single named edit above a marker, per Step 0.4) resolves it, and it runs even when Step 3.1's marker is already present, so it applied on the resume.
defects.output: run 1: `git check-ignore -v .run/README.md` -> '.gitignore:2:.run/' (exit 0; the probe requires exit 1); 12 of 13 probes passed. run 2 after Step 3.0: `git check-ignore -v .run/x` -> '.gitignore:64:/.run/*', `command grep -cx '\.run/' .gitignore` -> 0, and 13/13 probes pass — including `.run/README.md` trackable at Step 4's ✓ and committed at Step 5.
defects.fix: Already applied in the kit (Step 3.0 + the Step 0.4 exception + the troubleshooting row). Nothing further needed on the kit side; see the separate pa entry for fixing it at source.

defects.step: §4.4 — the governance .gitignore block (OPEN at source; mitigated by the kit's new Step 3.0)
defects.what: PA writes the directory form `.run/`, and git will not descend into an excluded directory, so any later re-include beneath it is unreachable. The kit now repairs this for kit-installed projects, but a PA-only install still cannot track anything under .run/ (its own §4 comment invites dated exceptions there).
defects.output: .gitignore lines 1-3 after §4: '# Project Architect 2.0' / '.run/' / 'project-architect-2.0/'; before Step 3.0, `git check-ignore -v .run/README.md` -> '.gitignore:2:.run/'.
defects.fix: Write the block as '/.run/*' + '!/.run/README.md' (+ 'project-architect-2.0/'), noting that the by-contents form is deliberate so later blocks can re-include tracked evidence under .run/. The kit's Step 3.0 then becomes a no-op (it already SKIPs when no bare '.run/' line exists).

defects.what: The audit command is not scoped to the installed tree, so it reports the installer packages' own template bodies and fails as literally written ('the ONLY acceptable hits are docs/project-architect.md and phase-ends/*.template.md'). It only looks clean if the agent's grep happens to honour .gitignore. The kit's Step 10.1 has since been given exactly this scoping and an explicit 'use a plain grep' instruction — PA's has not.
defects.output: command grep -rn '{{' --include='*.md' . -> 23 files, 20 of them under ./project-architect-2.0/ and ./decomp-architect/ (39 hits in ./project-architect-2.0/templates/PROJECT_CONTEXT.skeleton.md alone); Claude Code's wrapper grep -> 13 files, all but ./docs/project-architect.md under ./decomp-architect/.
defects.fix: Copy the kit's Step 10.1 wording: pipe through `grep -vE '^\./(project-architect-2\.0|decomp-architect)/'` and say the audit must be run with a plain grep, since a gitignore-aware wrapper silently narrows the result.

defects.what: '(then remove the __pycache__ it makes, or run it with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1)' — the second branch does not work: `python3 -m py_compile` writes the bytecode regardless, because writing it is the module's purpose. An agent trusting the env var leaves `tools/__pycache__` behind in a fresh install (untracked litter in an otherwise clean tree at the step's own final ✓).
defects.output: Controlled test, Python 3.12.3: `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m py_compile t.py` -> __pycache__ created; plain `python3 -m py_compile t.py` -> __pycache__ created. In the install: tools/__pycache__/audit_public.cpython-312.pyc appeared and was removed by explicit file + rmdir.
defects.fix: Drop the env-var branch and always remove the __pycache__, or replace the check with `python3 -c "import py_compile; py_compile.compile('tools/audit_public.py', cfile='/dev/null', doraise=True)"`.

defects.step: Step 10.1 — the allow-list vs prose that quotes the placeholder token (NEW, low severity)
defects.what: The audit cannot tell an unfilled placeholder from a document that legitimately QUOTES the token, and its allow-list holds only PA's spec and two templates. It fired twice in this dry-run on the installing agent's own writing — run 1 on phase-ends/CURRENT_PHASE.md (the milestone line quoted the audit command) and run 2 on phase-ends/PhaseEnd_Phase0.md (a verification line quoted `grep -c "{{PROJECT_NAME}}" …`). Both were rewritten in prose, which is the honest fix, but a real project's PhaseEnds, cookbook and decision log will quote the token routinely and every future install-time run of this lint will trip.
defects.output: run 2, first pass: the audit listed './docs/project-architect.md' AND './phase-ends/PhaseEnd_Phase0.md'; after rewriting that one line in prose: './docs/project-architect.md' only.
defects.fix: Either widen the allow-list to `./phase-ends/*.md` and the cookbook, or add one line to the step: 'a tracked document must never paste a literal double-brace — write the placeholder's name in prose', so the lint stays a true signal.

deviations: Run 1 stopped at kit Step 3.7 with the tree left as-is for diagnosis (2 commits, no Phase-0.5 commit); the coordinator fixed the installer and this run 2 resumed from Step 3 in the same throwaway repo, per Step 1.6's resume rule (first unticked checkbox). Steps 3.1–3.5 were idempotent: the .gitignore marker was already present so the append was SKIPPED, and the four firewall files were verified byte-identical to their templates instead of re-copied.

PA §6 (global assets under ~/.claude) SKIPPED ENTIRELY per the answers file (PA_HOME_DIRECTORY_STEP): no statusline copy, no ~/.claude/settings.json merge, no backup, no smoke test. Keys added to ~/.claude/settings.json: none. Verified after the run: the settings and statusline sha1s, the 81 memory files and the 25 ~/.claude entries are all byte-for-byte what before.txt recorded.
Gate 2 toggle skipped (unattended dry-run) — PA §8's Tier-1 '/effort max' prompt was not waited for; generation proceeded at the run's established depth.

Every developer question in both installers was answered from the answers file: PA §1 path (A), PA §5 dev interview, PA §8 Gate 1 ('nothing to adjust'), and the kit's Step 2 thirteen values + INSTALL_DATE. Nothing was invented; no key was missing.

Registry §E was generated as the intake's Part D asks — a single pointer line reserving G1–G65 — so PA's own '§E domain rules with corpus provenance' output was deliberately deferred; the kit then installed G1–G65 at offset 0, the fallback renumber never triggered.

Two of the installing agent's own documents quoted the placeholder token in prose and tripped the placeholder lints (PA's F9 in run 1 on CURRENT_PHASE.md; the kit's Step 10.1 in run 2 on PhaseEnd_Phase0.md). Both were rewritten in prose. PhaseEnd_Phase0.md is a Phase-A artifact and was therefore carried in the Phase-0.5 close commit, which is one path more than Step 10.7's list names — logged so the extra path is not mistaken for drift.

phase-ends/DIGEST.md also received a Phase-0.5 synopsis at close. Step 10.6 does not ask for one, but the digest's own maintenance rule ('at every PhaseEnd, append that phase's synopsis here') and the Phase-0 line the kit writes at Step 8.2 both do.

docs/decomp-ladder.md was NOT written: Step 1.3 found 'Governance and the firewall' in the constitution, so the intake had reached PA's generation step and the fallback branch never applied. It is therefore absent from the manifest rather than listed as SKIPPED (the manifest lists touched paths only).
tools/__pycache__ was removed with an explicit file deletion plus rmdir on absolute paths — never a relative rm -rf (Step 0.7).
LICENSE was written from the skeleton: it must be replaced with AGPL-3.0's verbatim text before the first push (carried in the kit's final message and the PhaseEnd's Deviations).

.claude/settings.local.json is invisible to git on this machine (the host's global ignore carries **/.claude/settings.local.json), so it neither committed nor showed as untracked. On a machine without that rule it would sit untracked at the end of the install, and neither installer names it as an intentionally-uncommitted item.

Copy-time and generation-time placeholders were substituted in place with sed/python on the cp'd templates rather than with the Edit tool; no template body was retyped from memory (SETUP §0.3's actual requirement). Block bodies were extracted verbatim from pa-overlays.md's fences.
Both installers' closing instructions to delete the package folder and start a fresh session were not followed, per the run brief.

Guardrail note: before.txt's `repo_dirty 0` reads 1 after the run because of the COORDINATOR's own uncommitted kit fix in the real tree (' M decomp-architect/SETUP.md', +17 lines adding Step 3.0, the Step 0.4 exception and the Step 10.1 scoping). The installing agent wrote nothing under /home/musashi/bfm-decomp outside the dry-run directory.
